about: Targeted per-language probes: the items where a grapheme model fails first,
assembled from the per-language research (each item names its class). Held-out
averages hide exactly these errors — the one controlled study that measured it
found grapheme and phoneme input indistinguishable on a held-out set and
Protocol: render each item, then (a) a native speaker marks binary pass/fail —
one hour per language, the highest-value evaluation money can buy here — and
(b) the ASR round-trip runs against the language's own floor (tools/eval_floors.json).
Items are inputs only: the correct pronunciations are what the native ear
carries, not what this file could encode.
